    INVESTIGATOR'S COMMENTS:
    2.     Invest~gations conducted in relation to the report made by
    Mr. WOODGATE on U.F.O. sighting revealed that the object seen by subject
    was probably an advertising aircraft promoting the opening or Canada' s
    wonderland. The airplane is a unique Cessna 172 owned by Mr. Gary McGUIRE,.
    President of Caribbean Freight Wings, ~oronto. It consists or ago rlashing
    lights installed on a frame underneath the wings of his Cessna and when the
    advertising sye~~m is on it is literally a flying billboard that can spell
    out slogans. Mr. McGUIRE showed me a film on his a~rplane in action. It
    appeared that beyond a quarter of a mile or depending •on the angle you see
    it at , t~e well-lit plane could easily appe~ to be a flying s aucer e~ape.
                                                                      I
    3.     According to McQUIRE ' s Aircraft Journey Log Book, on the 81-01-18 ,
    he took off rrom Brampton Airport with hie special Cessna at 1800 hours
    and .landed at Tot·onto IslanCl Ai:r-port at 1824 hours.   He took off again from
    Toronto lslan~ Airport at 1900 hours and flew over Yonge Street for more
    than one hour. He landed at Bramptcn Airport at 2030 hours. While flying
    over Yqoge Street, he was going North-South at 1 , 500 teet following the
    street. Mr. McGUIRE obtained an Air Carrier Operating Certificate #5063,
    and Air ~ransport Committee #3l33/80(c) and his Cessna is Class 7, Specialty
    (Aerial Inspection , Reconnaissance and Advertising)
